summary.text: The received analysis writes 些 with 此 above 二, while its attested uses include a line-final particle and the current senses “some” and “few.” The parts’ original roles and the link between these meanings are unresolved.

formation.text: The received Shuowen analysis records 此 above 二, but does not establish either part’s role in the original formation. The formation type is therefore disputed; modern shape and later phonetic-series listings do not prove an original sound or meaning contribution.

components.text: 此 is the upper element in the received analysis. Its role in the formation is unproven; later grouping with the 此 phonetic series does not establish that it supplied 些’s original sound.
二 is the lower element in the received analysis. The evidence does not establish that it contributes “two” or another meaning to 些.

history.text: The received Shuowen account analyzes 些 as 此 plus 二 and says its meaning is unclear. A scholarly article reports a sixth-century 玉篇 dictionary entry glossing it as “this” and “particle”; this is the earliest surviving dictionary record identified in that article, but its exact place in the graph’s history remains uncertain.

The transmitted 招魂 text uses 些 at line ends, where its commentary treats it as a particle. One proposal is that 些 replaced another graph in the poem’s transmission; other proposals link its graphic history with 告. These are competing explanations, and no early sequence is established.

uncertainties.text: The received 此-plus-二 account does not establish the original formation or the parts’ roles. The particle’s original written form is disputed, and no sound-based borrowing account is established.

senses.period: dating unresolved; attested in the transmitted 招魂 text
senses.text: The transmitted 招魂 text places 些 at line ends, and its commentary glosses it as a particle. This attests the transmitted spelling and commentary, not the poem’s original manuscript spelling or composition date.

senses.period: sixth century, as reported for a 玉篇 entry
senses.text: A scholarly article reports that a sixth-century dictionary entry glossed 些 as “this” and “particle.” The report does not establish which sense came first or identify an original meaning.
Current glosses include “little” and “few.” When this sense arose and how it relates to the particle or reported dictionary glosses are unresolved.
Current glosses include “rather” and “somewhat.” No historical development connecting these senses to another sense is established.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a chronological semantic link between the particle, the reported dictionary glosses, and the current quantifying or modifying senses.

overview.text: In the transmitted 楚辭 text, 些 marks line endings as a particle; today it can mean “some” or “few.” Its received written analysis places 此 above 二, though their original roles are unproven.

components.text: 此 is the upper element in the received written analysis; its original role is unproven.
二 is the lower element in that analysis; its contribution to 些 is unproven.

takeaway.text: The particle spelling in the transmitted 楚辭 text may postdate the poem’s original writing; its original graph remains disputed.

relationships.text: 二 is part of the received Shuowen analysis, but the evidence does not establish that it contributes “two” or another meaning. This records the proposed component analysis as disputed, not a confirmed semantic role.
